rows.stem: In one formula unit of salt ‘X’, seven molecules of water of crystallisation are present. The salt ‘X’ is :
rows.solution:
Green vitriol, ferrous sulphate heptahydrate, carries seven molecules of water of crystallisation in one formula unit: \(\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}\).

The others carry a different number: copper sulphate \(\mathrm{CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O}\) has five, washing soda \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\) has ten and gypsum \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\) has two.

So the salt is ferrous sulphate, which is option (C) \(\mathrm{FeSO_4}\).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The white light entering a glass prism, gets split into its constituent colours. It is observed that :

options.label: C
options.text: Yellow light deviates more than the blue light.

options.label: D
options.text: Green light deviates more than the orange light.

rows.solution:
The refractive index of glass is greater for light of shorter wavelength, so the different colours bend through different angles. Red light bends the least and violet the most, and the order of increasing deviation is red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

Green comes after orange in this order, so green light deviates more than orange light, which is option (D) Green light deviates more than the orange light.

rows.stem:
Consider the following circuits :

In which circuit will the power dissipated in the circuit be (I) minimum (II) maximum ? Justify your answer.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the three circuits (i) one 5 Ω resistor, (ii) two 5 Ω resistors in series, (iii) two 5 Ω resistors in parallel, each across a 12 V battery, are given only as drawings. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
The battery gives the same voltage, \(V = 12\) V, in all three circuits, so use \(P = \dfrac{V^2}{R}\): the power dissipated is inversely proportional to the total resistance.

Circuit (i): \(R = 5\,\Omega\), so \(P = \dfrac{144}{5} = 28{\cdot}8\) W.

Circuit (ii): the two resistors are in series, \(R = 5 + 5 = 10\,\Omega\), so \(P = \dfrac{144}{10} = 14{\cdot}4\) W.

Circuit (iii): the two resistors are in parallel, \(\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{1}{5}\), so \(R = 2{\cdot}5\,\Omega\) and \(P = \dfrac{144}{2{\cdot}5} = 57{\cdot}6\) W.

(I) The power dissipated is minimum in circuit (ii), which has the largest resistance.

(II) The power dissipated is maximum in circuit (iii), which has the smallest resistance.

rows.stem: Two lamps, rated 100 W; 220 V and 60 W; 220 V are connected in parallel to electric main supply of 220 V. Find the current drawn by the two lamps from the supply.
rows.solution:
In parallel each lamp gets the full 220 V, so each draws its rated current, \(I = \dfrac{P}{V}\).

100 W lamp: \(I_1 = \dfrac{100}{220} \approx 0{\cdot}45\) A.

60 W lamp: \(I_2 = \dfrac{60}{220} \approx 0{\cdot}27\) A.

The total current drawn from the supply is \(I = I_1 + I_2 = \dfrac{160}{220} \approx 0{\cdot}73\) A. (Adding the rounded values, as the marking scheme does, gives \(0{\cdot}72\) A.)

rows.stem: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. Use mirror formula to determine the position of the image formed in this case.
rows.solution:
For a concave mirror the focal length is negative, \(f = -20\) cm, and the object is in front of the mirror, \(u = -30\) cm.

Mirror formula: \(\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{-3 + 2}{60} = -\dfrac{1}{60}\).

So \(v = -60\) cm. The image is formed 60 cm in front of the mirror (on the same side as the object), so it is real and inverted.

rows.stem:
What happens when : (write balanced chemical equation)

(a) Lead nitrate is thermally decomposed,

(b) Natural gas burns in oxygen (or air) ?
rows.solution:
(a) Lead nitrate decomposes on heating to give yellow lead oxide, brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide and oxygen:

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO(s) + 4NO_2(g) + O_2(g)}\)

(b) Natural gas is mainly methane. It burns in oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water, with heat and light:

\(\mathrm{CH_4 + 2O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 + 2H_2O}\) + heat + light

rows.stem:
(a) Define one ampere.

(b) The resistance of a wire of \(0{\cdot}01\) cm radius is \(14\,\Omega\). If the resistivity of the material of the wire is \(44 \times 10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\), find the length of the wire. (Given \(\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\))
rows.solution:
(a) One ampere is the current that flows when one coulomb of charge passes through any cross-section of a conductor in one second: \(1\,\mathrm{A} = \dfrac{1\,\mathrm{C}}{1\,\mathrm{s}}\).

(b) Radius \(r = 0{\cdot}01\) cm \(= 0{\cdot}01 \times 10^{-2}\) m \(= 10^{-4}\) m, \(\rho = 44 \times 10^{-8}\,\Omega\,\mathrm{m}\) and \(R = 14\,\Omega\).

Area of cross-section: \(A = \pi r^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times (10^{-4})^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{m^2}\).

From \(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}\):

\(l = \dfrac{RA}{\rho} = \dfrac{14 \times 22 \times 10^{-8}}{7 \times 44 \times 10^{-8}} = \dfrac{44 \times 10^{-8}}{44 \times 10^{-8}} = 1\) m.

The length of the wire is 1 m.

rows.stem:
In one of Mendalian experiments, when \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation pea plants with round yellow seeds were self-pollinated, pea seeds with the following combinations were obtained in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation :

| Seeds | Round yellow | Round green | Wrinkled yellow | Wrinkled green |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number | 800 | 275 | 268 | 90 |

Analyse the result and describe the mechanism of inheritance of traits which explains the above results.
rows.solution:
Total seeds \(= 800 + 275 + 268 + 90 = 1433\). Dividing each number by the smallest, 90:

Round yellow \(\dfrac{800}{90} \approx 9\), round green \(\dfrac{275}{90} \approx 3\), wrinkled yellow \(\dfrac{268}{90} \approx 3\), wrinkled green \(\dfrac{90}{90} = 1\).

So the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) seeds are in the ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. This is the result of a dihybrid cross, in which Mendel followed two pairs of contrasting traits together.

Round (R) is dominant over wrinkled (r), and yellow (Y) is dominant over green (y). The parents were pure round yellow (RRYY) and pure wrinkled green (rryy). They give RY and ry gametes, so every \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plant is RrYy, with round yellow seeds.

When the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants self-pollinate, each forms four kinds of gametes in equal numbers, RY, Ry, rY and ry. Their random fusion gives 16 combinations: 9 round yellow, 3 round green, 3 wrinkled yellow and 1 wrinkled green.

Two of these, round green and wrinkled yellow, are new combinations not seen in either parent. Taken one trait at a time, round : wrinkled \(= 1075 : 358\) and yellow : green \(= 1068 : 365\), each about 3 : 1.

So the traits for seed shape and seed colour are inherited independently of each other.

rows.stem:
(a) Name the glands that secrete :

(i) Adrenaline

(ii) Thyroxin

(b) Explain with example how the timing and amount of hormone released are regulated in the human body.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal glands.

(ii) Thyroxin is secreted by the thyroid gland.

(b) The timing and amount of a hormone released are regulated by a feedback mechanism.

For example, when the sugar level in the blood rises, it is detected by the cells of the pancreas, which respond by producing more insulin. Insulin lowers the blood sugar level. As the blood sugar level falls, this too is detected by the pancreas, and insulin secretion is reduced.

rows.stem:
A saturated organic compound ‘A’ with two carbon atoms belongs to the homologous series of alcohols. On oxidation, it forms an organic acid ‘B’ with molecular mass 60 u. On heating ‘A’ with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K, an unsaturated hydrocarbon ‘C’ is formed.

(i) Name A, B and C.

(ii) Calculate molecular mass of C.

(iii) What happens when a pinch of sodium carbonate is added to compound B ? Write chemical equation for the reaction.

(iv) Draw electron dot structure of compound B.
rows.solution:
[CBSE marking scheme: the printed equation \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + Na_2CO_3 \rightarrow CH_3COONa + H_2O + CO_2}\) is not balanced (two sodium atoms on the left, one on the right); two molecules of ethanoic acid are needed, as below.]

(i) A, an alcohol with two carbon atoms, is ethanol, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\). On oxidation it gives B, ethanoic acid (acetic acid), \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\), whose molecular mass is \(2 \times 12 + 4 \times 1 + 2 \times 16 = 60\) u. Heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K, ethanol is dehydrated to C, ethene, \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\) (\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2}\)).

(ii) Molecular mass of ethene, \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\): \(2 \times 12 + 4 \times 1 = 24 + 4 = 28\) u.

(iii) Brisk effervescence is observed, because carbon dioxide gas is given off (it turns lime water milky):

\(\mathrm{2CH_3COOH + Na_2CO_3 \rightarrow 2CH_3COONa + H_2O + CO_2}\)

(iv) Ethanoic acid is \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}COOH}\). In its electron dot structure:

1. The methyl carbon shares one pair of electrons with each of three hydrogen atoms and one pair with the second carbon atom.

2. The second carbon shares two pairs with one oxygen atom (a double bond, C=O) and one pair with the other oxygen atom.

3. That second oxygen shares one pair with a hydrogen atom (the O-H group).

4. Each oxygen atom also carries two lone pairs, so every carbon and oxygen atom has eight electrons around it and each hydrogen two.

rows.stem:
(i) What is a homologous series of carbon compounds ? Write the name and formula of three successive members of the homologous series of compounds having functional group \(\mathrm{{-}COOH}\).

(ii) Write the name of two carbon compounds in which carbon atoms are arranged in the form of a ring. Draw the structure of any one of the two.
rows.solution:
(i) A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds that have the same functional group and similar chemical properties, with the same general formula, in which each successive member differs from the previous one by a \(\mathrm{{-}CH_2{-}}\) unit.

Three successive members of the series with the functional group \(\mathrm{{-}COOH}\) (carboxylic acids):

Methanoic acid, \(\mathrm{HCOOH}\)

Ethanoic acid, \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\)

Propanoic acid, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5COOH}\)

(Any three successive members are acceptable.)

(ii) Two carbon compounds whose carbon atoms are arranged in a ring are benzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\)) and cyclohexane (\(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}}\)).

Structure of cyclohexane: six carbon atoms are joined in a hexagonal ring by single bonds, and each carbon atom carries two hydrogen atoms.

(Benzene instead has six carbon atoms in a hexagonal ring joined by alternate single and double bonds, three of each, with one hydrogen atom on each carbon.)
